sources.title: Logarithmic Depletion of Vortex Stretching and Singularity Evasion in the 3D Navier-Stokes Equations
bound_claims: The selected consumer is explicitly restricted to a critical point singularity centered at one spatial point with vorticity magnitude locally O(|x|^-2).
The paper factors the critical profile as omega=Phi |x|^-2 with bounded shape factor Phi.
A stated structural consequence is that, for large lambda, the vorticity superlevel set A_lambda(t) is contained in one ball of radius R <= C lambda^-1/2 with C independent of time.
The paper defines the L^{p,infinity} Lorentz norm using decreasing rearrangement.

sources.title: On local Type I singularities of the Navier-Stokes equations and Liouville theorems
bound_claims: Type I suitable-weak singularity existence is equivalent to existence of a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with finite I.
I is the supremum of the scale-invariant A+C+D+E functionals over parabolic subcylinders.
The theorem is equation-specific; it does not by itself state the one-center critical-profile morphology consumed by Grujic v2.

scope_guard: No claim that the current cross-problem hostile fields solve Navier-Stokes.
No claim that Grujic v2 morphology follows from finite I.
No claim beyond the cited current primary-source surfaces.
